questions.question: Which nurse became known as the Lady with the Lamp?
questions.explanation: She cared for soldiers in the Crimean War and later set up a school for nurses in London.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink on its very first voyage?
questions.explanation: The Titanic hit an iceberg in the North Atlantic on its way from Southampton to New York.

questions.question: Who made the first powered aeroplane flight, in 1903?
questions.explanation: That very first flight lasted just 12 seconds.

questions.question: In which year did the First World War end?
questions.explanation: The fighting stopped at 11 o'clock on 11 November 1918, which is why we remember it on Remembrance Day.

questions.question: Who was Britain's Prime Minister for most of the Second World War?
questions.explanation: Churchill became Prime Minister in May 1940.

questions.question: What did Alexander Fleming discover in 1928?
questions.explanation: He came back from holiday to find mould had killed the germs on a dish he had left out.

questions.question: What were children called who were sent from cities to the countryside to keep safe in the Second World War?
questions.explanation: Evacuees carried a gas mask in a box and wore a label with their name on it.

questions.question: Whose refusal to give up her bus seat in 1955 started the Montgomery bus boycott?
questions.explanation: The boycott in Alabama lasted over a year and helped end segregation on the city's buses.

questions.question: In which city did a wall dividing the city in two come down in 1989?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall had split the city for 28 years.

questions.question: What did people in Britain celebrate with street parties on 8 May 1945?
options: The end of the war in Europe
questions.answer: The end of the war in Europe
questions.explanation: 8 May is VE Day, which stands for Victory in Europe.

questions.question: Who was the first person to reach the South Pole?
questions.explanation: Amundsen's Norwegian team got there in December 1911, about five weeks before Scott's.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
questions.explanation: In 1932 she landed in a field in Northern Ireland, surprising a farm worker.

questions.question: Which engineer designed the Clifton Suspension Bridge and the Great Western Railway?
questions.explanation: Brunel was famous for his tall stovepipe hat as well as his bridges, ships and railways.

questions.question: Who founded the Women's Social and Political Union to win women the vote?
questions.explanation: Her campaigners became known as the suffragettes.

questions.question: Which steam locomotive won the Rainhill Trials in 1829?
questions.explanation: Rocket reached about 30 miles an hour, which was astonishingly fast at the time.

questions.question: Which ship carried Charles Darwin around the world?
questions.explanation: The voyage, from 1831 to 1836, lasted almost five years.

questions.question: Which scientist was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences?
questions.explanation: She won for physics in 1903 and for chemistry in 1911.

questions.question: Which canal opened in 1869, linking the Mediterranean with the Red Sea?
questions.explanation: It saved ships the long voyage around the southern tip of Africa.

questions.question: Which country did Britain fight in the Falklands War of 1982?
questions.explanation: The war lasted 74 days, from April to June 1982.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web in 1989?
questions.explanation: He was working at CERN, near Geneva, which made the Web's software free for anyone to use in 1993.

questions.question: Which treaty, signed in 1919, ended the First World War between Germany and the Allies?
questions.explanation: It was signed in the Hall of Mirrors exactly five years after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

questions.question: What was the codename for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944?
questions.explanation: The landings began on D-Day, 6 June 1944.

questions.question: Which leader walked to the sea at Dandi in the Salt March of 1930?
questions.explanation: He walked about 240 miles to make salt from seawater, defying the British tax on salt.

questions.question: In which year was Nelson Mandela released from prison?
questions.explanation: He had spent 27 years in prison, and four years later he became South Africa's first Black president.

questions.question: Which supersonic airliner made its last passenger flights in 2003?
questions.explanation: Concorde could cross the Atlantic in about three and a half hours.

questions.question: In which year did women in the UK win the vote on the same terms as men?
questions.explanation: In 1918 some women over 30 got the vote, and the 1928 Act lowered the age to 21, the same as for men.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to take her seat as an MP in the House of Commons?
questions.explanation: Constance Markievicz was elected first, in 1918, but as a Sinn Féin member she refused to take her seat.

questions.question: Which engineer invented the bouncing bomb used in the Dambusters raid?
questions.explanation: He tried out the idea by skimming marbles across a tub of water in his garden.

questions.question: In which year did the Great Exhibition open in the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park?
questions.explanation: The Crystal Palace was later moved to Sydenham in south London, where it burned down in 1936.

questions.question: At which country house did Alan Turing and others break German codes in the Second World War?
questions.explanation: Its wartime work stayed secret until the 1970s.
